name: dex2jar
desc: Tools to work with Android .dex and Java .class files
why: Converts Android dex bytecode into Java jars, opening up APKs for inspection and poking.

brief.what_it_is: dex2jar is a set of command-line tools for Android .dex (Dalvik Executable) and Java .class files. The main tool, d2j-dex2jar, takes an APK or dex file and converts its bytecode into .class files packed as a jar, so the app can be read with ordinary Java decompilers. The toolkit also includes a dex reader/writer library with an ASM-like API, smali/baksmali disassembly and assembly, and d2j-decrypt-string for recovering obfuscated strings. The published executable list is longer and includes d2j-jar2dex, d2j-apk-sign, d2j-std-apk, d2j-jasmin2jar and others.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames it simply as tools to work with android .dex and java .class files. Its entry point is turning an APK into a jar that can be inspected.
brief.how_it_works: The README gives little detail on internals. It describes a dex reader/writer with a light-weight API similar to ASM, and a converter that writes .class files zipped as a jar. It also describes its smali/baksmali implementation as compatible in syntax with the original smali, with one extension: escapes in type descriptors such as "Lcom/dex2jar\t\u1234;".

commands_seen.context: Run from the repository root to build the distribution zip (the README says this produces dex-tools-2.1-SNAPSHOT.zip, about 5 MB).
Change into the build output directory that holds the distribution zip, before unzipping it.
Example usage from the README: converts the given APK. The output is written as apk_to_decompile-dex2jar.jar.

brief.install_notes: Not via brew alone. The README's documented route is to build from source: clone the repo, run ./gradlew distZip from the root (this needs a Java toolchain and the bundled Gradle wrapper), unzip dex-tools-*.zip from dex-tools/build/distributions, then run the d2j-*.sh scripts inside. Prebuilt downloads are on the GitHub Releases page. The brew formula lists 17 executables, which suggests a packaged install, but the README does not mention brew. No accounts or API keys are mentioned.
brief.standout: A reverse-engineering staple that pairs a dex-to-jar converter with the smali/baksmali assembler and a string decryptor, so one toolkit covers APK-to-Java inspection, patching the dex, and repacking. Its output is standard jars, so any Java decompiler can open the result.
brief.status: Maintained, with caveats. The GitHub Releases page lists v2.4 as Latest (tagged 'bugfix', published 03 Oct; the year is not shown in the fetched text), v2.3 (31 Aug, support for dex038 and dex039), and a v2.2 snapshot dated 2021-10-31. The README still says 2.1-SNAPSHOT, so it is out of date. The project moved from SourceForge, Bitbucket and Google Code to GitHub, and the old mirrors are marked 'old'.
brief.caveats: The README is short and partly stale: the usage section refers to dex-tools-2.1-SNAPSHOT and to running d2j-dex2jar.sh, while the release list is at 2.4. Output is a decompiled approximation, not original source, and the README does not discuss its limits. The README says the project is licensed under Apache 2.0. Installing from source needs a working Gradle/Java build. Sign-in and other navigation noise showed up in the releases page, but the release data was readable.
